name: The Small Court
setup: You are king of Anshan. It is not a large thing to be. A few valleys, a few households who answer when you call, and a much larger king in the north who expects his share.
teaches: A card you take stays with you for the whole match
disputed: Cyrus' court before the revolt is not described in any source. This mission is a scene, not a record.

name: Rally the Households
setup: Nobody in Fars keeps a standing army. You keep men who farm, and who come when they are called — if they think you are worth coming for.
teaches: Taking the same card twice makes it stronger
An army of one kind loses to its counter
disputed: That early Persian forces were household levies is inferred from the region and the period, not stated in a source.

name: Roads of Fars
setup: Grain moves slower than men do. Hold the road and you hold everything on it.
teaches: The ground you fight on changes what your army is worth
disputed: No supply action from this campaign is recorded. The mission teaches terrain using a plausible setting.

name: The Tribal Council
setup: The heads of the Persian tribes have come to hear what you intend. What you say to them decides who rides with you — and who does not.
teaches: Not every decision in a war is made on a battlefield

choices.label: Promise them the spoils
choices.reads: The riders come, and they come for what they can carry.

choices.label: Promise them standing
choices.reads: Fewer men, but the ones who come stay when it turns hard.

choices.label: Promise nothing you cannot give
choices.reads: They respect it. They are also slower to arrive.

disputed: Herodotus has Cyrus assemble the Persians and win them over with a day of labour and a day of feasting. It is a good story and a late one; the council here is invention built on it.

name: Border Warning
setup: A Median column has come as far as the passes. Not to conquer — to remind you what is above you.
teaches: The counter triangle decides more than raw numbers
disputed: No border action is recorded before the main campaign.

name: A Kingdom Divided
setup: Not everyone in Fars wants this fight. Some of your own would rather pay the tribute and keep the harvest.
teaches: A wide army holds together longer than a deep one
disputed: Persian opposition to the revolt is not attested. It is likely rather than known.

name: The Refusal
setup: The tribute is due. You are not sending it. Everything after this happens because of a thing you did not do.
teaches: A war can begin with a refusal rather than an attack
disputed: That the revolt began with withheld tribute is the Greek tradition. The Babylonian evidence records only that Astyages mobilised against Cyrus.

name: The First Advance
setup: Astyages has taken the field himself. His army is larger than yours, better equipped than yours, and has done this before.
teaches: Being outnumbered is a problem you draft your way out of
disputed: That Astyages campaigned in person is in the Nabonidus Chronicle. The course of the advance is not.

name: Broken Ground
setup: You cannot beat this army on open ground. So do not fight it on open ground.
teaches: Choosing where to fight is choosing half the result
disputed: The gorge here stands in for terrain the sources do not describe. The Persian Gates itself belongs to a different war two centuries later.

name: Retreat to Persis
setup: You are not going to win today. Today you are going to still have an army tomorrow.
teaches: Winning is not always the same as destroying the enemy
An army that survives a bad day can fight a better one
disputed: No withdrawal is recorded. The mission exists to teach that a loss can be survived, which is the honest lesson of most campaigns.

name: The Camp Holds
setup: Standards, grain, and the families who followed the army. Lose the camp and the army stops being an army.
teaches: A shield wall holds ground it cannot chase
disputed: Camp defence is a standard feature of ancient warfare, not a recorded episode of this campaign.

name: Divided Loyalties
setup: Word comes that not all of the Median army wants to be here. Harpagus commands its centre, and Harpagus has reasons of his own.
teaches: Armies are made of people who can decide things
disputed: Harpagus' grievance and his role are Herodotus, heavily novelised, and centuries later. That the Median army changed sides IS in the near-contemporary Babylonian record — the motive is not.

name: The Plain before Pasargadae
setup: Open ground on the Murghab plain. Nothing is built here yet. Everything that will be built here depends on tomorrow.
teaches: Where a capital stands is decided before it is built
disputed: That the decisive fighting happened at Pasargadae comes from Strabo, about five centuries later.

name: The Last Stand
setup: Astyages is in the field with everything he has left. So are you.
teaches: How the Achaemenid Empire was founded
An army can decide a war by refusing to fight it
disputed: The Nabonidus Chronicle — near-contemporary — records that Astyages' own army mutinied, bound him and handed him to Cyrus. The pitched battle is the Greek version of the same events.
